That pass is recorded below in full, including two apparent discrepancies I investigated and found sound rather than reporting.

advisories.title: v25 changes nothing outside the review-bookkeeping machinery, now the thirteenth consecutive generation
advisories.observation: Partitioning the v24 to v25 leaf diff, zero substantive paths changed and nothing was removed anywhere; the sole change is the rewrite of registerCoverageRule.subjectDigestIdentity. The authorization content is unchanged and BLK-1 through BLK-4 remain STILL-ROUTED. The artifact has grown from 71101 bytes at recorded v8 to 150719 bytes, with essentially all growth in the machinery governing its own review; registerCoverageRule now carries seventeen named members and there are five further GOVERNING rule objects beside it. I record this a fifth time with one addition that bears on disposition rather than defect: the identity chain the last twelve generations were spent closing now terminates at measured file bytes on both the review branch and the subject branch, so the line of inquiry that produced nearly every finding since v14 appears exhausted rather than merely quiet.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: An observation about where review effort has gone, not a defect. Every bookkeeping finding across these thirteen generations has been real, including six of mine and eleven of Codex's, and nothing has regressed. Offered because a coordinator weighing whether this candidate is converging on DR-105 and DR-114, and whether further generations are likely to be productive, should have the measurement rather than the impression.
advisories.suggestedDisposition: None required of this artifact. Offered for coordinator awareness only.

advisories.title: Three advisory subjects remain substantively unaddressed from v11 through v25
advisories.observation: FC-SUBTYPE-CLASS still exercises no CA-3 row despite CA-3 carrying the largest subtype domain including the deferred KEYCHAIN; destinations.actionSubtype still mixes record and serialized class vocabulary in its requiredness clause before restating it serialized; coveredActs still keys the host classes as CA-1-host-head and CA-4-host against the record vocabulary. Both reviewers have raised all three across fourteen generations, all correctly registered ADVISORY-NON-BLOCKING and correctly absent from the repair arrays.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: These remain the case my calibration deliberately leaves advisory: the governing rule is complete and only its fixture population or phrasing is short. Codex has independently graded the same three advisory in every round they have appeared.
advisories.suggestedDisposition: Optional. One CA-3 accept row and one CA-3 cross-class refuse row would close the first at negligible cost.

advisories.title: The FC- prefix is shared by failClosed condition ids and acceptance fixture class ids
advisories.observation: failClosed's six required conditions are identified FC-C1 through FC-C6, and the twenty-six acceptance fixture classes are identified FC-FAIL-CLOSED, FC-CARRIER-SHAPE, FC-SUBTYPE-CLASS and so on. Both live in the same FC- namespace, and prose references resolve only by context: doctorV4FieldMapping.destinations.actionSubtype ends 'matching nullWhen and FC-C5', which a reader or a tool scanning for fixture ids will take as a fixture class. This tripped my own enumeration, which reported FC-C1 through FC-C6 as referenced-but-undefined fixture classes until I checked and found them to be failClosed conditions.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: No GOVERNING rule mechanically enumerates FC- ids, unlike findingIdRule which governs the finding-id namespace, so the collision is documentary rather than load-bearing and nothing is currently mis-resolved. Recorded under the discipline I adopted at v17 that friction in my own tooling should be surfaced rather than silently worked around, and because the analogous collision in the honestyRepairsFrom namespace was adopted as a repair at v18.
advisories.suggestedDisposition: Optional. Renaming the failClosed conditions to a distinct prefix, or stating that FC-C[0-9]+ denotes a failClosed condition and FC-[A-Z]+ a fixture class, would remove the ambiguity.

verdictBasis: The dispatch permits ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. This review returns 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, so the verdict is ACCEPT. The single claimed repair is complete and verified by execution rather than by reading: subjectDigestIdentity now requires the canonical subject file to exist, measures its bytes, and anchors both the recordedInputs pin and the register's subjectSha256 to that measured digest, which refuses the exact case my v24 finding named where two recorded values are both wrong but agree. It is total over all eighteen rounds and thirty-six lanes, and with it the identity chain terminates at measured bytes on both the review branch and the subject branch. Because that closes the line of inquiry which produced nearly every finding since v14, and because an exhausted line yields the same silence as a sound artifact, I spent the substantive effort where I had not looked since v19: the authorization content itself. That pass found the per-class subtype lists agreeing in all three places they appear, every declared count matching its structure, BLK-1 through BLK-7 accounted for, and all eleven D-032 property pins answered, including the slice-1 egress execution side assigned rather than returned unsettled. Two apparent discrepancies surfaced and both proved sound on inspection; I record what they were and why I did not raise them. Custody is clean on every pin, all 77 recorded inputs reproduce, and the full corpus from v6 through v24 passes every stated check with zero failures. I state plainly that my ACCEPTs in this lineage are 0 for 3 and that those verdicts stand unrevised; that record is a reason to search harder, which I did, but it is not a reason to withhold a verdict the evidence supports.
